137830.overview:
Fury is a variant of the arcade game Time Pilot, and was programmed by Timothy Purves.

The player is the sole defender of a small South American country that is being overtaken by communists and has to shoot down as many enemies as possible before the CIA steps in. Like in the arcade game the player is in control of a plane that can move and shoot in multiple directions. Among the enemy forces there are airplanes, helicopters and hot balloons that can be shot down and parachutes that have to be rammed. As the game goes on it gets harder with the addition of magnetic air mines. These will chase the player who has to dodge them. The first one appears after scoring 5,000 points but the amount increases at higher point values. After scoring 30,000 points the player's air cannons heat up making it necessary to fire slower.

137915.overview:
Frogger is a single-player and multiplayer action arcade game. The objective is to guide a frog safely from the bottom of the screen to one of several goal slots at the top. Each attempt requires crossing a busy multilane road filled with cars, trucks, and other vehicles, then navigating a hazardous river filled with floating obstacles. A successful run places the frog into one of the home slots, and once all are occupied the player advances to the next, more difficult level.

The road portion is the first challenge. Vehicles move at varying speeds, and contact with any of them instantly costs the frog a life. Once across the pavement, the frog must contend with the river, where the water itself is deadly. The frog rides on moving logs, turtles, and other floating objects to cross. Some turtles periodically dive beneath the surface, forcing careful timing. Alligators and snakes appear on higher levels, with their heads being dangerous to touch.

The home slots at the top of the river present their own challenges. Only empty slots can be occupied, and some may be blocked by alligator heads. Occasionally a lady frog appears on a floating object, and safely escorting her to a home awards bonus points. Flies sometimes appear inside goal slots, also offering a scoring bonus when captured. Each level is completed by filling every slot before the timer runs out.

Scoring is based on survival and efficiency. Points are earned for every forward movement, successfully guiding a frog home, escorting the lady frog, eating flies, and surviving longer durations. The game ends when the player runs out of lives.

Different releases of Frogger introduced different changes. The original arcade cabinet supported one or two players alternating turns, while early home ports to systems such as the Atari 2600, ColecoVision, and Intellivision recreated the core gameplay with graphical compromises. Later console and computer versions sometimes altered level design, added new obstacles, or provided enhanced visuals and sound. Digital re-releases and compilations preserved the original arcade experience, while modern remakes experimented with updated graphics and new modes but retained the central premise.

169216.overview: Fruity is a computerized version of a fruit slot machine developed by Impsoft and published by Dragon Data Ltd. in the UK and Eurohard in Spain in 1983.

175574.overview:
Froglet is a 1-player Frogger clone for the Dragon 32/64.

The player controls a frog that moves in cardinal directions, trying to cross two busy highways with cars traveling in opposite directions. The roads are separated by a river with moving lily pads that the frog must hop across. There are six homes at the top of the screen that the player tries to position their frog into. The player starts with five lives, and the game restarts if all are used.

175575.overview: The football management game style has been one of the most enduring since Kevin Toms pioneered it in 1982. You start in the 4th division with the team of your choice, and can play on indefinitely in the hope of reaching the top division and dominating it, as well as winning the cups. Players can be bought or sold, with their transfer values varying according to the size of any bid. Their skills and morale vary as the season goes on, with resting key players in easy matches often a key move. You can take out a loan, limited depending on your division, while day-to-day bills must be covered. Matches feature short animated highlights sequences of key moments (Text only for C16).

175576.overview:
Inscrutable oriental electronic strategy!

Play a friend, the computer, or let your computer play itself. You can challenge and play at up to four different levels.

175577.overview:
Flight is a 1 - 5 player landing simulator.

The player attempts to follow a flightpath in real time in the vertical and horizontal dimension to safely land on a runway. There are 4 levels of difficulty, which introduce crosswinds, and on the highest level the player has to fly by instruments only. If the player misses the runway, they're fined and can try again. If they land short, the plane crashes.

175585.overview: After receiving a mysterious message Dan Diamond, PI, travels to the indicated address to find a large crypt looming out of the darkness of an eerie graveyard. The door is open but as Diamond steps forward the ground gives way and Diamond finds himself trapped in Franklin's Tomb. As Diamond you must unlock the puzzle of the tomb and escape, but will escape bring you closer to the one who is asking for your help?

175606.overview: As Dan Diamond, PI, you awake on a sandbar in the middle of an ocean with no company but the space ship you skilfully landed at the end of Lost in Space. The ship refuses to talk, except to mumble about learner drivers and to tell you to go away. So denied entry to the ship and any conversation there seems little else to do but go swimming. Perhaps civilization is closer than it looks and maybe, just maybe, you will find the one who sent you the message that got you into this mess.

175609.overview:
The object of the game is to rescue the occupants possessions from the burning building by using the lfits to reach the various levels but avoiding the fireballs.

All objects must be collected before you may progress to the next stage of the game. Freddy will lose one bucket of water if he falls into the cauldron or hits a fireball. Extra buckets are awarded every 1000 points. When all buckets of water have been used the game ends.

At the top of the screen is a Thermometer which, if it reaches zero, will cost a bucket of water.

175703.overview:
A financial strategy game for 2 to 6 players.

A Spanish version of this game was released by Eurohard as Fabrica de Chicles.

421333.overview:
Franklin in Wonderland is the fourth text adventure featuring Dan Diamond, private investigator.

Waking up from taking a snooze after eating a large cucumber sandwich in the woods, the player finds that everything has changed. Dan Diamond is transported to Wonderland, and post solve numerous puzzles related to the famous book. Contains puzzles involving changing size and numerous random events.

446485.overview: Just like Spinnaker's FaceMaker, A.S.K.'s Facemaker is about making faces. You start out by entering the person's name and sex, and from there on, you are asked questions about face, eyes, facial hair, complexion and so on. Jewellery and hats are also options. Once a face has been completed, you may change it or draw another one.

446494.overview:
Fairground Fantasy is a text adventure with additional arcade elements for the Dragon 32/64.

The young boy Ivor has gone missing at the fairground. The player must find and rescue him. Initially played as a simple text adventure, the player uses text commands to move about the fairground and pick up and use items to solve puzzles. The player starts their adventure with only 6 pence, and must make money and receive clues by besting arcade sequences involving the various fairground games. These include a roulette wheel, pulling objects from a barrel, and test of strength. Ali-Kebab's Magic Carpets will randomly transport the player around the fairground. It's game over if all money is lost.

446495.overview:
Fantasy Fight is a 1-player arcade game for the Dragon 32/64.

As an enthusiastic but inexperienced and ill-equipped adventurer, the player has persuaded a powerful wizard to magically transport them to a fabled labyrinth. Within this mystical maze it is rumored that bags of gold lie around for the taking, and it is said that magical weapons and spell scrolls of enormous power are scattered about.

The player controls a small character that moves between rooms collecting treasures while avoiding a number of enemies. Points are awarded by defeating enemies and collecting bags of gold. The player starts with five lives, and their health is displayed by a sword at the bottom left of the screen. There are three different colors of keys which can be picked up to open appropriately colored doors. The player can also pick up spells and weapons which are used to defeat enemies.

446532.overview:
The player is a passenger of a light aircraft on a normal domestic flight, when suddenly the pilot is taken ill. They are the only person left on the plane who has any chance at all of bringing it down safely. The player can choose to take the final landing approach, or full simulation where the player must navigate the plane to the landing site.

Played from a 1st-person perspective, the player must use their throttle and elevator to control speed and altitude. The aircraft has a maximum speed of 400 knots, and will stall below 130 knots. The player can control flaps to reduce stalling speed as they get within five miles of their destination, but if they go too fast at full flap or the landing gear engaged the plane will be damaged.
